description:
Goal: make root submission a root query, not a global source-publication driver. `submit_root` must stop enqueueing `ScopeCode` for every known `CodeId`; source publication belongs to `ScopeCode(code)`, runtime prelude visibility belongs to the first non-runtime `ScopeCode` dependency on `CodeScoped(runtime_prelude)`, and the root should grow only by reading/waiting on the facts required by its entry.

Grounding:
- `northstar.html` says parsing/top-level discovery is eager only at the code-contribution boundary, runtime prelude is ordinary compiler-owned code text, and the first non-runtime `ScopeCode` waits on `CodeScoped(runtime_prelude)` before scoping user code against the saved prelude head.
- Current `World::submit_root` enqueues `ScopeCode(code_id)` for every `self.code.ids()` before `SeedRoot(root)`. That gives root submission source-tier authority it should not have.
- Fresh `fz2 --log-telemetry` traces for the fz-eak callable fixtures show the consequence: one tiny user file plus one runtime root schedules `ScopeCode(CodeId(0))` five times and `ScopeCode(CodeId(1))` six times before Kernel is pulled; the prelude macro function sources `fn`, `fnp`, `defmacro`, `defmodule`, `defprotocol`, and `defimpl` are each noted four times. This is broad phase-shaped work, not fact-driven reachability.

Signal / acceptance targets:
1. Add telemetry-observing tests around the small callable/runtime fixtures or equivalent minimal programs. Tests must assert job-span and source-publication counts from telemetry, not internal maps alone.
2. Per compile world, `IndexCode(code)` should process each submitted code contribution at most once unless the code contribution is actually new. For the single-user-file callable fixtures, expected indexed code ids are: user source once, runtime prelude once when first needed, and Kernel/runtime module source once only if a reached reference requires it.
3. Per compile world, completed source publication for a `CodeId` should happen once. The same `FunctionSource(function)` fact must not be re-noted when its aggregate value has not changed. Specifically, the six prelude macro source facts (`fn/1`, `fnp/1`, `defmacro/1`, `defmodule/2`, `defprotocol/2`, `defimpl/2`) should be observed exactly once each, not four times.
4. Root submission should not directly enqueue `ScopeCode` for all known code ids. A root may wait on the entry facts it needs and enqueue/follow up the smallest source work that can prove those facts; unrelated submitted user code must stay cold and must not publish function sources merely because a root exists.
5. Runtime module pull-through remains lazy. A program using only `+` may pull Kernel, but it must not lower/analyze unrelated Kernel functions. If the current source surface still notes the whole Kernel interface once, that is acceptable for this ticket only if it is explicitly captured as remaining module-granularity work in a follow-up ticket; this ticket must not hide repeated prelude/user source publication behind that deferral.
6. Assertions should distinguish job attempts that only wait from jobs that actually publish facts. If wait-only retries remain, telemetry/tests must make that visible and bounded; the hard correctness target is no repeated unchanged source publication.

Required change shape:
- Move authority to the right tier. Do not add an adapter/shim/compatibility path.
- Prefer a source/root fact boundary that makes the broad `for code_id in self.code.ids() { ScopeCode(code_id) }` loop unnecessary by construction.
- Update `.agent/docs/pipeline.md` and/or `.agent/docs/modules.md` if the repair sharpens the documented source/root handoff.

Verification:
- Focused telemetry tests proving the targets above.
- Existing source/root laziness tests stay green, including late code after root not reseeding semantics and unused definitions staying cold.
- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the relevant compiler2 lib tests.
title: Compiler2 source/root ownership: root submission must not scope every code contribution
